result:
result: Spec bullets and role text are met, with one blocking contradiction (`visual-judging` still says to start the shared server first) and five non-blocking items. I read the files and did not run `mise run verify`, so no test results are covered.

findings (paths under `/home/user/holyagent-feat-dev-server-targets/`; dist = `packages/integrations/claude/dist`):

Spec bullets, all in `dist/skills/dev-server/SKILL.md`:
- Detection with the signal used: met (L11-13).
- Target record fields: met. All five spec groups are present, and "address" is widened to URL, session, display or device (L17-23).
- Unique names: met (L25).
- Owner-only stop: met (L48-50). The record carries the owner, and the stop command is checked against it.
- Each platform with interchangeable tools: met (L37-42). Tools are called examples at L9 and L35.
- `[verify]` notes: met as one blanket sentence (L35). The spec says to mark flags against installed versions, and no individual flag is marked. Non-blocking.
- Environment matrix: met (L46), word for word with the spec.
- Blocked report with reason and unblock: met (L46) and in `dist/agents/worker-operations.md:19`.
- Closest honest substitute, and "web build is not native render": met (L46).

Role text (spec deliverable 3):
- Worker.operations (`dist/agents/worker-operations.md:19`): met. It reads the record, uses unique names, reports the completed record and whether it started or reused the target, reports blocked, and stops only what it started.
- Worker.visual (`dist/agents/worker-visual.md:15`, `:17`): met. It reads the record, never a bare URL, starts no target, and reports blocked when no record is named or the target is down.
- Reviewer.visual (`dist/agents/reviewer-visual.md:17`): met. It has no shell, judges captures from Worker.visual or Worker.operations, and reports blocked without a record or captures.
- Root (`dist/agents/holyagent.md:178`): met.

Blocking:
1. `dist/skills/visual-judging/SKILL.md:15` (source `packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/visual-judging/SKILL.md:14`) says "For web work, start the shared server first".
   - It misses spec Part C deliverable 3 and the brief's check for contradictions with untouched text. It limits the target to web work and names a "server", so the root can skip the target for TUI, desktop and mobile work.
   - Fix: "Start the render target first, per platform (the `dev-server` skill)."

Non-blocking:
2. `dist/agents/holyagent.md:113` (source `root/assignments.md:12`) says "(rounds, shared server, images)", and `visual-judging` no longer states a shared-server rule beyond item 1. Fix: replace with "render target".
3. `dist/skills/dev-server/SKILL.md:31` says "Reviewer.visual has no shell and judges those captures". `specialist/interface-inspection.md` still lets it inspect a web target live through the browser tools, and `reviewer-visual.md:17` allows this for web. Fix: "judges those captures, or for web inspects the URL through its browser tools".
4. `dist/skills/dev-server/SKILL.md:35` repeats "Tools are examples" from L9, so the rule appears twice. Fix: drop the first clause at L35 and keep "flags change between versions, so [verify] each against the installed one".
5. `dist/agents/worker-operations.md:19` says "in the fields of the `dev-server` skill", but Worker.operations cannot call Skill. The skill covers this at L30 by having the brief name the file path, so the role text depends on the root following that. Fix: "in the fields the brief lists".
6. `docs/pi/claude-parity.md:49` says "(a running app or a served static build)", which is stale after the widening. Line 113 says the plugin ships two skills, but this is pre-existing and the plugin now has seven. Fix: "a running render target" at L49, and correct the count at L113 only if you want it in scope. `docs/development.md:84` only lists skill names, so it has no contradiction.

Unrequested: none found. The diff also edits `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/usage.md`, `requirements.md`, `agents.ts` and the tests, which fits deliverable 3 and the requirement-phrase sync.
